title: Grateful Dead Live at The Auditorium on 1970-02-23
lineage: SBD > MR > Cass > DAT > CDR > EAC (secure) > Cool Edit (minor fixes) > CD Wave (retracking) > mkwACT > SHN (seekable)

ai_review.summary: Fair‑quality soundboard capture of a fragmented 1970 show with standout acoustic gems (Little Sadie, Seasons of My Heart, Me & My Uncle) and an unexpected Not Fade Away burst.
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard source that suffers from muddiness, hum between songs and occasional mic distortion, giving it a fair overall fidelity. Musically the set shines on the intimate acoustic numbers – Little Sadie, Seasons of My Heart, Me & My Uncle and a surprising Not Fade Away jam – though listeners note that large portions of the concert are missing, making the flow feel disjointed.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the acoustic performances and highlight several songs, but many point out significant recording flaws and missing portions; weighted scoring yields a mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers describe the tape as slightly muddy, with hum between tracks, occasional Bobby McFerrin mic distortion and uneven, somewhat mono‑ish mix; a few cut‑outs (e.g., Mason's Children) are noted.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set appears to be a mid‑show fragment, sandwiched acoustic numbers between electric material; missing opening and closing sections make the pacing feel uneven despite strong individual performances.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers note his sunburst Strat (gnarlier tone) and a broken string moment; he calls out bandmates and trades licks during the jam.
band_member_comments.Phil: His bass is highlighted as driving the train on Not Fade Away, providing strong momentum in an otherwise uneven mix.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pigpen’s organ on Not Fade Away receives praise for finally being audible; his vocal solo on Me & My Uncle and a humorous “yellow dog” joke are also mentioned.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ work is noted as low but present, unusual for early‑70 shows where keyboards were often buried.
